title: Objectwise invariance of homotopy-cartesian squares
statement: Use small simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy-cartesian squares in the two-leg fibration-replacement sense specified in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition]. Let squares with corners $(Q,X,Y,Z)$ and $(Q^{\prime},X^{\prime},Y^{\prime},Z^{\prime})$ be strictly commutative. Suppose maps $Q\to Q^{\prime}$, $X\to X^{\prime}$, $Y\to Y^{\prime}$, $Z\to Z^{\prime}$ commute with every edge of the squares and are all weak homotopy equivalences. Then the first square is homotopy cartesian if and only if the second square is homotopy cartesian. All eight simplicial sets may be non-Kan or empty.
